name: Miami International
subtitle: Stand assignment and push control for Central Base, Concourses D-J, D60, E Remote and West Cargo
source: Stand positions and headings, taxiways, aprons and buildings from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL); gate and bay list, spots, frequencies and restrictions from the Jeppesen 10-9B and 10-9C (10 APR 26) and 10-9E (24 MAY 24) charts (user-supplied). The chart frames are generated: north up, 1.5 m per pixel, linear in lat/lon. Each OSM stand is 20 m back from the terminal end of its lead-in line (the end nearest the OSM gate node of that number, else the end nearest a building), but never more than 30 m out from the gate node. D60 and E Remote stands were checked against satellite imagery. Only gates the charts list are kept (OSM D5A, D9A, D28A, D60D, H3A, C113-C116 are left out). Central Base was renumbered on 10-9B: each chart label takes the nearest OSM stand, and C100-C105 sit at their chart labels. Cargo City (W10-W19B) sits at its 10-9E labels, nose to the building, because OSM still has the pre-2024 numbering there; W55, W61B, W68 and W78 are placed between their chart neighbours. A gate whose A line ends within 12 m of its base line is one stand labelled with both (D8/A, F15/A, J17/A); G5A and G7A have no OSM line and share G5 and G7. Spots are placed from the charts' 0.1' grids. UPS and FedEx stands on the north side are OSM's (nose stop at the stand's node, aircraft 20 m behind); N66-N74 and N87A, which OSM lacks, come from the scenery's stand map fitted to OSM's (OSM's N88 is the scenery's N87A). Hangar 890 and the Northeast Base ramp come from the Jeppesen Northeast Base chart (user-supplied, to scale, ~0.87 m/px): stand-line midpoints and the label end as the nose, which OSM's lead-in lines agree with where they share a name; the north side has its own generated frame (MNE), north of MIA's.

airlinesSource: Approximate, from miami-airport.com and airport guides: American and its Eagle flights on Concourse D, D60 and E, oneworld partners on E, Delta on H, the other US and Canadian carriers on F and G, foreign carriers on J, F and H, cargo on West Cargo. Worth checking against current use. E Remote, the J Bays and the AA Cargo Area are not given out automatically. FedEx and UPS park on their own north-side ramps (N54-N74, N87-N95).
notes: Positive apron control and pushbacks: spots 0-4 on 128.025 (Miami Gates); 5-10 on 130.325 (American Apron Control); 11, 12 and 16-21 on 130.5 (Miami Gates); 13-15 on 130.95 (American Apron Control); 22-28 on 132.375 (Miami Gates).
Pushback clearance required: gates D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D14; D60K, D60M, D60P, D60V, D60W; F16, F18, F19, F23.

Aircraft with a wingspan greater than 171 ft (52 m) may not taxi on Twy P east of Twy U, except ADG VI aircraft (214 ft / 65 m or greater) complying with the Miami ADG VI operational plan when the adjacent airside service road is closed.
West Cargo: spots 73 and 75 on 121.8 (Miami ATC). Cargo City and the AA Cargo Area have no frequency on 10-9E: no CTC line in their telex.
The charts give apron frequencies per spot; which gates each frequency covers is inferred from the spots next to them.
UPS Ramp (N87-N95) and FedEx Ramp (N54-N74), north side along Twy K: no published spots or frequencies, so their telex has neither.
Northeast Base and Hangar 890 (spots 52-54): the chart gives no frequency, so their telex has no CTC line. These stands are remote/maintenance parking and are not given out automatically.
